title: — Pronouns with لِ and بِ

quizzes.title: Exit Ticket · Final Quiz — everything, mixed Score: 0 /8

blocks: ## What you will be able to do by the end
### Objectives
- Attach all pronouns to لِ — with the fatḥah switch and the لِي exception Writing
- Attach all pronouns to بِ — with the kasrah chain ( بِهِ، بِهِمْ ) Reading
- Use لِ for having and giving: لِي أَخٌ، هَذَا لَكَ Speaking
- Use the star phrases أَهْلًا بِكُمْ and مَا بِكَ؟ in conversation Listening
### Success Criteria
- 🟢 I can say لِي، لَكَ، لَهَا، بِكَ and use لِي أُخْتٌ to say what I have.
- 🟠 I can build all twelve forms of each family — and explain why لِ becomes لَـ everywhere except لِي .
- 🟧 I can apply the kasrah chain ( بِهِ، بِهِمَا، بِهِنَّ ) and describe people with لَهَا / لَهُ .

[callout] Why this matters in the exam These two families carry enormous exam weight: لِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ is THE way to list your family in Speaking; أَهْلًا بِكَ opens every role-play; هَذَا لَكَ gives every gift; and Reading texts lean on بِهِ / بِهَا ("with it") constantly. You met لِي in the Age lesson and مِنْ فَضْلِكَ at the souq — today the whole system behind them unfolds.
## The لِ family — to, for, and having — اللَّامُ

On its own, لِ carries a kasrah: لِمُحَمَّدٍ — for Muhammad. But the moment a pronoun jumps on, the lām straightens its back into a fatḥah : لَكَ، لَهَا، لَنَا . One single form refuses to change — the very first one.
### Master Grid Twelve forms of لِ

[callout] The superpower: "I have" 🎁 Arabic has no verb "to have" — لِ does the job: لِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتَانِ. — I have a brother and two sisters. لَنَا بَيْتٌ جَمِيلٌ. — We have a beautiful house. لَهَا صَدِيقَاتٌ كَثِيرَاتٌ. — She has many friends. Literally "to me is a brother" — belonging expressed as direction. You've said لِي since the Age lesson!

[callout] Whose? Mine! 🔁 Lesson 2's lost-property question returns with its short answer: — لِمَنْ هَذَا القَلَمُ؟ — هَذَا لِي! / هَذَا لَهَا. And gift-giving: هَذِهِ الهَدِيَّةُ لَكَ — this present is for you. Eid vocabulary, ready to go. 🌙
## The بِ family — with and by — البَاءُ

Where لِ changed its vowel, بِ is stubborn: the kasrah stays put in all twelve forms. But that steady kasrah has a consequence — remember Lesson 2's "shy ḍammah"? Here it triggers on every ه -form: بِهِ، بِهِمَا، بِهِمْ، بِهِنَّ .
### Master Grid Twelve forms of بِ

[callout] What بِ does all day كَتَبْتُ بِالقَلَمِ → كَتَبْتُ بِهِ. — I wrote with it. سَافَرْنَا بِالسَّيَّارَةِ → سَافَرْنَا بِهَا. — We travelled by it. أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِكُمْ! — Welcome, all of you! Tools, transport, and the warmest word in Arabic hospitality.

[callout] The caring question 💙 مَا بِكَ؟ / مَا بِكِ؟ — What's wrong? What's the matter with you? Literally "what is with you?" — the first thing a good friend asks. Answer: لَا شَيْءَ، أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ — nothing, I'm fine (literally "in goodness" — another بِ !).
## The rules, side by side — القَوَاعِدُ
Three clean rules govern everything on this page — including the answer to last lesson's cliffhanger.
### Grammar A Rule 1 — the lām straightens (except for me)

[callout] لِ → لَـ with every pronoun… except لِي لِمُحَمَّدٍ (kasrah before a noun) → لَكَ، لَهَا، لَنَا، لَهُمْ (fatḥah before a pronoun) → لِي (the one keeper) Why does لِي resist? The ي of "me" loves a kasrah before it — the same reason كِتَابِي ends -bī . The lām bends to the pronoun it carries.
### Grammar B Rule 2 — the bā's kasrah chain

[callout] بِ never changes — so هُ must بِهِ · بِهِمَا · بِهِمْ · بِهِنَّ — but بِهَا stays (the ا shields it) Lesson 2's "shy ḍammah" ( فِي بَيْتِهِ ) was a preview; here it's the main event. After any kasrah, the هُ -family politely matches. The ك -forms and ـنَا never flip — only the ه -core listens.
### Grammar C Rule 3 — no bodyguard needed

[callout] The cliffhanger answered 🔍 Last lesson: why رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي and not ✗ لِنِي ؟ Because the guarding nūn protects verbs only. Prepositions behave like nouns — plain ـي , no bodyguard: VERB: سَاعَدَنِي (nūn on duty) · NOUN: كِتَابِي · PREPOSITION: لِي، بِي (no nūn) Three homes, one family, and now you know the complete dress code for each. 🗝️
## Having & welcoming — المِلْكِيَّةُ وَالتَّرْحِيبُ
The two prepositions run two of the most useful conversations in Arabic: لِ lists what you have and describes people, and بِ welcomes guests and checks how they are. Here they are in full flow.
### Grammar D The two everyday exchanges

[callout] "Tell me about your family" 🏡 — هَلْ لَكَ إِخْوَةٌ؟ (Do you have siblings?) — نَعَمْ، لِي أَخٌ كَبِيرٌ وَأُخْتَانِ صَغِيرَتَانِ. (Yes, I have a big brother and two little sisters.) — وَهَلْ لَكُمْ بَيْتٌ فِي المَدِينَةِ؟ (And do you have a house in the city?) — لَا، لَنَا شَقَّةٌ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنَ المَسْجِدِ. (No, we have a flat near the mosque.)

[callout] Describing people with لَـ لِ also gives qualities and possessions to others: لَهَا شَعْرٌ طَوِيلٌ. — She has long hair. لَهُ صَوْتٌ جَمِيلٌ. — He has a beautiful voice. لَهُمْ تَارِيخٌ عَظِيمٌ. — They have a great history.

[callout] Heritage link 🌟 These words fill your day: الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ — praise be to Allah ( لِ + اللّٰه ); بِسْمِ اللهِ — with the name of Allah ( بِ ); أَهْلًا بِكُمْ at every door; and بِخَيْرٍ whenever someone asks how you are. Urdu shares the welcome too — āp kā khair maqdam — the same open-hearted بِ .
## 🎮 The Gift Post — لِمَنْ؟ بِمَاذَا؟

Eid packages are flying through the post — each needs the right label. The card tells you the situation; you pick the correct لِ or بِ form. Watch the fatḥah switch, the kasrah chain, and the welcome rounds! Eight rounds. 👥 Breakout teams: the sorting office champions win.
## لِ and بِ in the real exam — فِي الاِمْتِحَانِ
Three disguises: an Eid letter in Reading (having, giving, welcoming), have-you-got lines in Listening, and the family & hospitality questions in Speaking.
### Task A · Reading 📖 An Eid letter — رِسَالَةٌ فِي العِيدِ

[callout] عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ يَا صَدِيقِي! أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي بَيْتِنَا غَدًا. لِي هَدِيَّةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ لَكَ — أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ تُعْجِبَكَ. عَائِلَتِي كُلُّهَا هُنَا: لِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ، وَلَهُمْ هَدَايَا لَكَ أَيْضًا! جَدَّتِي أَعَدَّتِ الحَلْوَى، وَسَتُرَحِّبُ بِكُمْ جَمِيعًا. هَلْ لَكُمْ سَيَّارَةٌ؟ إِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ، فَلَا تَقْلَقْ — سَنَأْتِي بِهَا إِلَيْكُمْ.
- What does the writer have for his friend, and which words say so?
- How many siblings does the writer have? Quote the لِ phrase.
- Who else has gifts for the friend — and which pronoun proves it?
- سَتُرَحِّبُ بِكُمْ — who is being welcomed, and is it "you" or "them"?
- Detective: سَنَأْتِي بِهَا — what does بِهَا refer to? (Not a person!)
- A beautiful gift — لِي هَدِيَّةٌ… لَكَ : "I have a gift… for you" (both prepositions in one line).
- Three — لِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ (two brothers + one sister; the dual أَخَوَانِ counts as two).
- The siblings — لَهُمْ هَدَايَا لَكَ : "they have gifts for you", ـهُمْ pointing back to them.
- "You all" — بِكُمْ (addressed plural). Grandmother will welcome the friend's whole family.
- The car — سَيَّارَة is feminine, so "we'll come with/in it" uses بِهَا . The friend's transport worry is solved!
### Task B · Listening 🎧 Who has what?
Listen without looking first. Ask a partner or reader to say each line twice , then write who has it, who is welcomed or what is used.
### Task C · Speaking & Writing ✍️ Your family & your welcome — دَوْرُكَ!
Excellent speaking-practice territory. Answer aloud 🎙️, then write, using at least four لِ / بِ forms .

[callout] Examiner prompts هَلْ لَكَ إِخْوَةٌ وَأَخَوَاتٌ؟ — Do you have brothers and sisters? مَاذَا لَكَ فِي غُرْفَتِكَ؟ — What do you have in your room? كَيْفَ تُرَحِّبُ بِضُيُوفِكَ؟ — How do you welcome your guests?
## Choose your challenge
Pick one level. Due next lesson via Teams Assignments. ✍️
### 🟢 Mild
Make a two-column chart : all twelve لِ forms beside all twelve بِ forms, fully vowelled — highlight لِي (the kasrah keeper) and every بِهِ -type flip in a different colour.
### 🟠 Spicy
Write ten sentences : five saying what you and your family have ( لِ ) and five welcoming guests or naming tools/transport ( بِ ) — include one مَا بِكَ؟ exchange and at least one kasrah-chain form.
### 🟧 Hot

Write an Eid welcome letter «أَهْلًا بِكُمْ» in the style of the reading text: invite a friend's family, list what you have for them, and welcome them warmly — at least ten لِ / بِ forms , each underlined and labelled (family · rule).
## Review, consolidate, and finish 🏆
Eight questions, all mixed. 6+ = success criteria met. 💬 Scores in the chat!
